chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Jamil, who said:
I asked Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام) about the words of the Mighty and Majestic:
'He it is Who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers' [48:4]
He (عليه السلام) said: 'It is the iman (faith).'
He (the narrator) said: '(And what about) "and He has supported them with a Spirit from Him"' [58:22]
He (عليه السلام) said: 'It is the iman (faith).'
And (he asked) about His words: 'and He necessitated for them the word of taqwa (piety)' [48:26]
He (عليه السلام) said: 'It is the iman (faith).'

key_terms.السَّكِينَةَ: Tranquility; the divine peace sent down into the hearts of the believers (48:4), interpreted by the Imam as iman
key_terms.الْإِيمَانُ: Faith; the Imam's consistent and authoritative interpretation of all three Quranic concepts under discussion
key_terms.بِرُوحٍ مِنْهُ: A Spirit from Him; the divine support bestowed upon the believers (58:22), interpreted as iman
key_terms.قَوْلِهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: The words of God, the Mighty and Majestic; the standard formulaic phrase used to introduce Quranic citations for exegesis
key_terms.قُلُوبِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The hearts of the believers; the locus into which God sends down the sakina according to 48:4
key_terms.كَلِمَةَ التَّقْوَى: The word of taqwa (God-consciousness/piety); the divine obligation mentioned in 48:26 and equated with iman

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) say the sakina, the Spirit from God, and the word of taqwa signify in the Quran?
ai.summary: Jamil narrates a question he posed to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) regarding three Quranic phrases — the sakina (tranquility) sent into believers' hearts [48:4], the Spirit with which God supports them [58:22], and the word of taqwa He made incumbent upon them [48:26]. In each case the Imam gives the same authoritative interpretation: all three divine gifts are, at their essence, iman (faith), revealing a unified Quranic theology of faith as the root of spiritual peace, divine assistance, and God-consciousness.

en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Yunus from Jamil who has said the following:
“Once I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) about the words of Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious,
‘It is He who has sent serenity (al-Sakinah) into the hearts of the believers.’ [48:4]
1 then asked about, ‘ . . . and supported them with a spirit from Him. . . .’ [58:22]
I asked him about the words of Allah, ‘He made them to accompany piousness. . . .’ [48:26]
